g.text: Respiratory rate from thermal video: processing pipeline

text.style: font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #444444

g.text: Demonstrated on SYNTHETIC breathing added to a real thermal recording (see footer). Lepton-like 160×120 frames, 7.5 fps, 120 s clip.
added to every frame (inset: first 20 s).
Region warped to a fixed grid in
is hidden under the static level,
Per pixel: remove level + trend. SVD
splits the pixels into patterns; keep
Spectrum peak = rate. SQI = share of
Rate every 5 s (30 s windows) vs the
injected rate. With real data: vs the

Synthetic data disclosure: frames 2090–2989 of SIM1 participant T001, practice drive (Taamneh et al., Sci Data 2017; FLIR Tau 640, downsampled to 160×120). No breathing signal could be found in these frames, so a smooth

temperature pulse (max 0.3 °C, rates 12/18/24 breaths/min with ±5% variation) was added just below each nostril in software. It is a test signal, not a model of real breathing; results show the pipeline works, not that breathing can be measured.
Not yet implemented: selecting the closest person (single person in view) and masking camera recalibration (FFC) and motion outliers. Frame rate 7.5 fps assumed (unresolved for SIM1).
